findings.claim: V2 canManage() returns hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so an all-groups VIEW-only permission grants global group manage (privilege escalation).
findings.evidence: GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (GroupsResource.java:181) gates only on auth.groups().requireManage(); a view-only admin can create top-level groups and, with rep.id set, move any group to top level via realm.moveGroup(child, null). canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires MANAGE only; GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:75 javadoc copies the same VIEW-or-MANAGE wording. Reasoned; test sketch: createAllGroupsPermission(policy, Set.of(VIEW)) then realmAdminClient groups().add(...) expects 403, reasoned to return 201.
findings.reason: Raised independently by all four seats with concrete call-path evidence; authz escalation from a read scope to a write path. Red test: VIEW-only admin creating a top-level group must get 403.

findings.claim: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs and only ever sees the all-groups type resource, breaking user search/count for group-scoped admins.
findings.evidence: Per-group resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource without a type, so findByType(server, "Groups") returns only the type resource; the code passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission (findByName misses, falls back to type resource) and adds that UUID to the set. All-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS: UserModel.GROUPS={type-resource UUID} in UsersResource.searchForUser (398/425/430/448) and BruteForceUsersResource:147 -> /users empty. Per-group VIEW_MEMBERS only: empty set -> getUsersCount(realm, emptySet) returns 0 (JpaUserProvider.java:600) while /users returns members via post-filter; first/max applied before canView filter gives short pages. V1 (GroupPermissions.java:313-315) uses the resource and resource.getName(). Reasoned; test sketches: all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS then users().search(null,-1,-1) contains alice; per-group VIEW_MEMBERS then users().count()==1.
findings.reason: All four seats traced the same type/ID mismatch with source citations; functional breakage of user listing and count. SP rated Critical; normalised to Important because it denies rather than leaks access.

findings.claim: hasPermission evaluates either the per-group resource or the all-groups type resource, never both, so once any per-group permission exists for group G, all-groups grants no longer apply to G.
findings.evidence: DefaultPolicyEvaluator adds type-level policies only when resource.getType()!=null and per-group resources have no type; findPolicyIdByNullResourceScope excludes policies with defaultResourceType. Patch also removed the canViewGlobal short-circuit in GroupsResource:113/GroupResource getSubGroups so every listing goes through canView(g). Contradicts the javadoc 'permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups' and the test comment 'fallback to all-groups permission'. Same pattern pre-exists in UserPermissionsV2. Reasoned; test sketch: all-groups VIEW for myadmin + per-group MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP on topGroup for another user, then groups().group(topGroup).toRepresentation() should succeed (reasoned 403).
findings.reason: Two correctness seats independently reached it via the policy evaluator; not rejected (no contrary citation). Red test needed before fixing; if it cannot be made red, defer as unverified.

findings.claim: When group G has no per-group resource, evaluating the all-groups type resource also pulls in every per-group permission, so a VIEW permission on group A grants VIEW on every group without its own resource; the resourceId filter UserPermissionsV2 uses to prevent this is missing.
findings.evidence: OCR: type resource has type="Groups" so findByResourceType (PolicyEntity.java:64, defaultResourceType) returns per-group permissions too, and DecisionPermissionCollector.onComplete grants scope-permission scopes without containsResource. PT: UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission filters permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()) (added in c2acddc7ca to stop a single-user grant granting all users); the Groups copy omits it. Reasoned; test sketch: per-group VIEW on myGroup for myadmin + all-groups MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP for another user, groups().groups() should be size 1, reasoned 2.
findings.reason: Correctness seat's evaluator trace is corroborated by the advisory seat's diff against the sibling UserPermissionsV2 guard; potential authorization leak. Kept at Important (reasoned, not reproduced); red test decides.

findings.claim: hasPermission is a third near-copy of the V2 evaluator (UserPermissionsV2:94-133, ClientPermissionsV2:207-235) and the copies have already diverged.
findings.evidence: Copies differ in the resourceId filter (see the leak finding); one shared hasPermission on MgmtPermissionsV2 would remove ~60 lines.
findings.reason: ponytail: advisory refactor spanning pre-existing Users/Clients code outside this change; fix the missing filter locally first.

findings.claim: requireManageMembers javadoc says it throws when canManageMembership is false; implementation checks canManageMembers.
findings.reason: Javadoc added in this patch contradicts the code; one-word fix.

findings.claim: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission javadoc says '@return Stream of IDs' but the method returns Set<String>.
findings.reason: Javadoc added in this patch is wrong; trivial.

findings.claim: canView() javadoc says 'Or if it has a permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups' without the 'For V2 only' qualifier that canList/canManage carry; V1 canView() checks roles only.
findings.evidence: Inconsistent with sibling javadoc in the same interface added by this patch.

findings.claim: Deleting a group under FGAP v2 leaves its per-group authz resource and permissions orphaned; the GroupRemovedEvent cleanup is registered only for V1 and no V2 replacement or group synchronizer exists.
findings.evidence: AdminPermissions.registerListener (73-98) is gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ v1; GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws; AuthorizationStoreFactory synchronizers cover clients, realms, users only.
findings.reason: Spec gap with no spec to confirm scope; likely follow-up work for an EXPERIMENTAL feature. Settle by deleting a group with a V2 permission and checking the resource store.

findings.claim: The V1 feature check moved from event time to listener registration time, so runs that enable V1 at runtime (@EnableFeature skipRestart=true) never register the role/client/group-removed cleanup listener.
findings.evidence: Legacy testsuite UsersTest.java:228/235/258/295 and token-exchange tests enable ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ with skipRestart=true. Production unaffected (Profile fixed at boot). PT and SP judged the refactor behaviour-preserving for production; MP flagged it as an unrelated behaviour change.
findings.reason: Test-environment-only effect; settle by running the legacy UsersTest FGAP cases with skipRestart and checking for orphaned resources after role/client/group removal.

findings.claim: No migration adds the Groups type resource and new scopes to realms whose admin-permissions client was initialised before this change; init() returns early when the client exists.
findings.evidence: getResourceTypeResource returns null, then policyStore.findByResource(server, null) NPEs (JPAPolicyStore.java:215), giving HTTP 500 on group checks for admins without MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS roles; creating group permissions fails with 'Scope does not exist'.
findings.reason: FGAP v2 is EXPERIMENTAL with no upgrade guarantee; settle by starting on a realm initialised at the base commit and calling a group endpoint as a non-role admin.

findings.claim: getResourceName is not extended for GROUPS, so group permission resources render a null display name and the type resource lacks an 'All groups' label.
findings.evidence: Used by PolicyResourceService.java:218 when listing a permission's resources; USERS branch has the equivalent handling.
findings.reason: Small, direct gap in the new resource type's wiring.

findings.claim: switch(resourceType) throws NullPointerException for a null resource type where the old if-chain threw IllegalStateException.
findings.evidence: updateResources (RepresentationToModel.java:1423) calls this for any admin-permissions policy with resources set; only ScopePermissionRepresentation is validated to carry a resource type.
findings.reason: Both paths are server errors on invalid input; only the exception type changes. Settle by posting a non-scope policy with resources and no resourceType.

findings.claim: No tests cover all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS, users().count(), VIEW-only write attempts, or mixed all-groups and per-group permissions; testManageGroupMembership asserts only the positive case.
findings.evidence: testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers passes only through the post-filter path; testViewGroups grants VIEW but never attempts a write.
findings.reason: These are the red tests for the Critical/Important findings above.

findings.claim: try(Response)+assertEquals(CREATED)+ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse is redundant now that handleCreatedResponse asserts 201 and closes the response (also lines 194-199, 260-265).
findings.evidence: test-framework ApiUtil.java:8-14 was changed in this patch to assert and close; line 165 already uses the one-liner.
findings.reason: Advisory deletion, ~9 lines, no behaviour change.

findings.claim: New test file nits: copyright year 2024 on a 2025 file, stray ';;' at line 68, typo 'initializaed' in the @BeforeEach comment.

Patch includes changes not directly related to the feature, against CONTRIBUTING.md/PR-CHECKLIST.md: AdminPermissions listener restructure, ApiUtil rewrite, removal of ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes, UserPermissions canManageDefault/canViewDefault inlining (and RolePermissions), AdminPermissionsSchema switch/reorder, GroupResource 'child = null', unused import in UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest.
findings.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md 'No changes to code not directly related to your PR'; PR-CHECKLIST.md same.
findings.reason: Most items are removals of methods that lost their callers with the V1/V2 interface split (PT grepped: no remaining callers) or helpers used by the new test; splitting them out buys nothing reviewable. Minor advisory standards finding.

findings.claim: New Groups resource type and scopes (manage-membership, manage-members, view-members) ship without documentation.
findings.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Includes documentation'; fine-grain.adoc covers V1 only.
findings.reason: FGAP v2 is EXPERIMENTAL and the prior Users/Clients v2 work is likewise undocumented; belongs with the feature's docs pass.
